ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in Figure 1, E is a point on side BC of the equilateral $\triangle ABC$ (not coinciding with points B and C). Draw AE, and construct an equilateral $\triangle AEF$ to the right side using AE as its side. Draw CF. It is known that the function relationship between the area ($S$) of $\triangle ECF$ and the length ($x$) of BE is shown in Figure 2 (P is the vertex of the parabola). What is the side length of the equilateral $\triangle ABC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} It is known from the diagram that the maximum value of $S_{\triangle ECF}$ is $2\sqrt{3}$,\\
$\therefore \frac{\sqrt{3}}{16}a^{2}=2\sqrt{3}$\\
Solving gives $a=4\sqrt{2}$ or $a=-4\sqrt{2}$ (discard)\\
$\therefore$ The side length of equilateral $\triangle ABC$ is $\boxed{4\sqrt{2}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In Figure 1, ABC is an equilateral triangle, B, E, C are on the same horizontal base, and E is between BC; connect AE, and construct equilateral triangle AEF on the right side with AE as a side, point F is on the right side, and CF is also connected in the figure. Figure 2 is the graph of the parabola of S with respect to x, the horizontal axis is x, the vertical axis is S, the parabola opens downward, and the vertex is labeled P; a dashed line is drawn from the vertex to the vertical axis, and the corresponding height on the vertical axis is labeled 2√3, so the maximum area given by the graph is S_max=2√3. Reasoning: Let the side length of equilateral triangle ABC be a. Establish a coordinate system: B=(0,0), C=(a,0), A=(a/2,√3a/2). Since x=BE, E=(x,0). Constructing equilateral triangle AEF on the right side of AE is equivalent to rotating vector EA clockwise by 60° about point E to obtain EF. Vector EA=(a/2-x, √3a/2), and after rotating clockwise by 60°, we get (a-x/2, √3x/2), so F=E+(a-x/2, √3x/2)=(a+x/2, √3x/2). In triangle ECF, EC is on the x-axis, and the base EC=a-x; the height from point F to the x-axis is √3x/2. Therefore the area S=1/2·(a-x)·(√3x/2)=√3/4·x(a-x). This is a quadratic function of x opening downward, and its maximum value is attained when x=a/2: S_max=√3/4·(a/2)(a/2)=√3a^2/16. From Figure 2, S_max=2√3, so √3a^2/16=2√3, a^2=32, a=4√2 (the side length is taken as positive).
